description: The observer in `¬begins(after($x), term)` reads the original input through the span projection. The chosen a elides T at 0 and at 2, so the reconstructed input is T A B T, and c reads both synthetic T as bare terminals. a survives only if after($x) is the empty original suffix; then a and c are two readings. Read over the reconstructed tokens, after($x) begins with the trailing synthetic T, which term reads, a is lost, and c alone would pass (engine §7.5).
grammar:
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision elision-only
%rule text a | b | c
%rule a [+T="ta"] $x(pair) [+T="ta"]
%conditions ¬begins(after($x), term)
%rule b [+T="ta"] [+T="ta"] pair [+T="ta"]
%rule c T="ta" pair T="ta"
%rule pair A B
%rule term T
